method: Who is on the sheet: every listing in Coinbase's x402 Bazaar index with 3 or more unique payers in 30 days on the day of the run (real demand). The index is the list of where to look; every verdict comes from the seller's own endpoint.

How each listing is asked: an unpaid GET, then an empty JSON POST if the GET did not answer 402, from a public address, following no redirect. A listing that gives no payable offer is asked once more a few seconds later and the second answer is kept. A listing whose offer differs from its listing (a higher dollar price, a missing dollar option or another pay-to address) is asked once more a few seconds later, and both answers are kept (seen.again). When its dollar price is higher and its offer gives an example input in its discovery block (extensions.bazaar), the second ask sends that example (a query on a GET, a JSON body on a POST, at most 16,384 bytes) and seen.again.request says seller_example. Nothing is ever paid.

answer: payable when the endpoint answered 402 with at least one payment option naming a network, an asset, an amount and a pay-to address (the x402 v2 PAYMENT-REQUIRED header or the v1 body); unreadable_offer for a 402 without one; no_payment_asked for a 2xx; gone for 404 or 410; http_4xx and http_5xx for other errors; unreachable when no HTTP answer came; declined when the URL is not public https, so it was not asked; not_asked when the run reached its per-host cap or time budget before asking it; other for anything else.

Dollar options: an option is a dollar option when its network and asset are USDC on Base, Base Sepolia, Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, Avalanche, World Chain, Monad or Solana, by contract (the list is part of this rule). Every other option is floating: its dollar value moves, or is not known to this rule.

Comparing one listed option: the live options on the same network, asset and scheme are its candidates (on the same network and asset, any scheme, when none has the same scheme). Its price is above_listed when any candidate asks more than every amount the listing states for that network, asset and scheme (a buyer agent may be asked to pay it), else as_listed when a candidate asks exactly the listed amount, else below_listed when the cheapest asks less. Its pay_to is as_listed when every candidate pays an address the listing states for that network, asset and scheme, different when any does not, not_listed when the option names no address.

price of the row, from the listed dollar options only: not_listed when the listing states no usable price; not_dollar when it states no dollar option; listed_option_missing when no listed dollar option has a candidate; else above_listed when any compared dollar option is above_listed, else below_listed when any is below_listed, else as_listed.
floating of the row: the same verdict from the listed floating options only, null when the listing states none. It is reported so the sheet hides nothing, and it is never held against the seller.

pay_to of the row, from every compared listed option (an address does not drift): different when any is different, else as_listed when any names an address, else not_listed; listed_option_missing when no listed option has a candidate.

Confirmation: when the endpoint was asked twice, a price, floating or pay_to that the two answers do not both give is varies, and is not held against the seller. When the second ask sent the offer's example input and the first answer's price was above_listed but the second's was as_listed or below_listed, the price is input_priced: the endpoint quotes by its input, and the higher quote to an empty request is a ceiling, not an overcharge.

matches_listing: true when the price is as_listed or below_listed and the pay_to is as_listed; false when the price is above_listed or listed_option_missing or the pay_to is different; null otherwise (no payable offer, nothing in dollars listed to compare, input_priced, or a verdict that varies). A false says the live offer differs from the listing, which can also mean the listing is out of date; it is not a finding of bad faith.
network: testnet_only when every live payable option is on a test network, else mainnet.

asked: the live option compared with the first compared listed dollar option (listed options in sorted order), or with the first compared listed option when no dollar option is compared. differs: up to 8 compared listed options whose price is not as_listed or whose pay_to is different, dollar options first, each with its listed and live amount and address and whether it is a dollar option.

Networks are compared as CAIP-2 ids (x402 v1 names are mapped; a reference longer than 32 characters is cut to 32), EVM addresses in lower case, other addresses as written, amounts as whole atomic units.

Strict formats: a field that does not look like what it is is dropped, so that no seller can put a sentence into a signed sheet. A network must be a CAIP-2 id or an x402 v1 name; a scheme a short word; an asset or address hex after 0x, or letters, digits and . _ : - only, at most 80 characters; a pay-to on an EVM network a 20-byte address. An option missing a field is not payable. The example input sent is never kept.
why: Sheet-1 compared each listed and live amount in the asset's own units. A seller who prices in dollars and quotes XRP or another floating token at the day's rate was counted above its listing whenever the index was a few days old, and more than half of the listings this sheet counted as differing were that drift, not a higher price. Sheet-2 judges price on dollar options only (USDC on ten networks, by contract), reports every other option's price apart as floating, and holds a different pay-to address against a seller on any option, since an address does not drift. The original sheet is unchanged and still verifies under sheet-1.
